- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mean to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — apply a 3–5% downward bias to first 7–10 days.  
- After a strong upward move in forecast, the true outcome often corrects downward within 5–7 days — apply a 2–4% downward adjustment to subsequent days.  
- When sentiment is consistently high (e.g., > 0.7 over 3+ days), model tends to overfit recent trends — apply a 3–5% mean reversion adjustment toward prior 10-day average.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by > 2% over 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
